passage: Teacher's note, Class 4. On Monday Bharati was made to stay in during play for breaking the classroom clock, which she did not do. I believed it was true because the clock fell when I was out of the room. After school Raghav, her classmate from the same row, came to my desk with his bag on his shoulder, looking at the floor. He said quietly, "Sir, it was not Bharati. A ball hit it. I saw." He added that he was scared to say so. I thanked him and told him it took courage. Next morning I spoke to Bharati, apologised and asked the boys who threw the ball to own up. Hemant Sir.

qa.q: What was Bharati made to stay in for?
qa.a: She was made to stay in during play for breaking the classroom clock.

qa.q: What does Raghav's looking at the floor while he spoke suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he was nervous and scared to speak up, though he wanted to help Bharati.

qa.q: What could Raghav do if a classmate is blamed unfairly again?
qa.a: He can quietly tell a teacher what he saw, as he did, and perhaps ask a friend to come with him if it feels too scary.

qa.q: How might Bharati have felt when Hemant Sir apologised?
qa.a: Bharati probably felt relieved and cleared, and grateful that Raghav had spoken up for her, though she may still have felt hurt from being kept in.

grounding: A teacher's note on a classmate who quietly spoke up for a child punished for something she did not do.
